assessment.nobel_worthiness: Physiological discovery of GLP-1 as an incretin and glucose-dependent insulin secretagogue, followed by its translation into durable agonists for type 2 diabetes and obesity, is a rare chain from basic physiology to transformative therapy. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact (glycemic control, weight, emerging cardiovascular and renal benefit) are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst for GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans, Drucker for the biology of GLP-1/GLP-2 action and translation, Mojsov for peptide identification and synthesis of the active form. Knudsen is a strong drug-development contributor but a prize limited to three people must leave her out or reduce basic-science credit. Priority and credit among early GLP-1 contributors is contested and the list may omit relevant individuals.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy confirmed by many large independent trials and wide real-world use; the mechanistic interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Contested allocation of credit among Mojsov, Holst, Drucker and others in the early peptide work
Four credited names cannot all be honoured; the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) would be omitted
Long-term safety of chronic therapy is still being characterized, and I cannot verify every historical detail independently

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The concept is original and the clinical consequences are large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early costimulated CAR design, June the clinical translation in CLL and ALL, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and gene-engineered T cells in patients. Other early CAR originators (not on this list) may deserve consideration, so the configuration is plausible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several independent trials confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers. Limitations remain in solid tumors, toxicity and access, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Early CAR concept credit (e.g. Eshhar and others) is outside this credited set
Efficacy in solid tumors is unproven
Whether the three listed names fairly represent the decisive contributions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic identification of SMN2 exon 7 splicing as a correctable defect and its use through an antisense oligonucleotide yielded the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a fatal motor neuron disease. Clear mechanism, clear clinical outcome, and a platform for RNA-targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer for splicing mechanism and ASO design principles, Bennett for oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development. A two-person prize is coherent. The role of the SMN1 gene discoverers (not in this list) is a separate, earlier recognition question.
assessment.maturity: Approved and used since 2016 with years of follow-up, and with confirmation of benefit across infants and later-onset patients. Mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Relative weight of basic splicing work versus chemistry and clinical development
Long-term outcomes in treated patients are still accumulating
Other contributors in the program may have claims not captured in the list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated microbial channels expressed in defined cell types give millisecond causal control of neural activity and have become a standard tool across neuroscience and beyond. Discovery of channelrhodopsin function and its adaptation to neurons is original, with immense methodological impact on circuit analysis.
assessment.attribution: Discovery of channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and demonstration in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, also Miesenböck's earlier work) make credit difficult. A three-person limit forces hard choices, and Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have substantial claims.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for two decades; early clinical use in vision restoration is just emerging. As a tool rather than a therapy the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among six credited people is unresolved
Primarily a tool; direct medical benefit is still early
Whether a prize for method fits the Physiology or Medicine criteria as strongly as for a disease-level discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable condition and was the proof of principle for kinase-targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. The earlier discovery of the BCR-ABL fusion lies outside the supplied credit and may reduce the prize's novelty framing.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data and many independent confirmations; very mature, perhaps in danger of seeming late.
uncertainties: Medicinal-chemistry credit may extend beyond named people
Overlap with earlier recognition of the oncogene and fusion biology
Whether the Committee views this as sufficiently distinct from earlier cancer-gene prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in lesions and cancer incidence. A major preventive discovery with global public-health consequences.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller for L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity, Frazer for the vaccine concept and early development. Other groups (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer and industry teams) have claims that may complicate a fair three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Population-level outcomes from many countries confirm protection against lesions and now cancers. Stable and mature, with some precedent for HPV-related recognition already.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among the VLP developers
Overlap with the earlier prize for HPV and cervical cancer
Whether credit supplied here fully covers the decisive contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term culture of self-renewing adult stem cells as three-dimensional organoids that preserve tissue architecture opened new routes for disease modeling, personalized testing and regenerative approaches.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid work, with Sato as the first author of the key culture methods. A two-person configuration is coherent and well documented.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and widely replicated; clinical and translational applications remain early, so medical impact is still maturing.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is still largely prospective
Contributions from other organoid pioneers (outside the list) may be raised
Possible premature recognition relative to ultimate clinical use

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation, first described in the hippocampus, together with NMDA-receptor dependence and behavioural links to memory, provides a foundational cellular model of learning. Strong originality and conceptual influence.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo for the original discovery, Morris for linking NMDA-dependent plasticity to spatial learning. Collingridge for NMDA-receptor dependence is also strong, forcing a hard choice among four.
assessment.maturity: Replicated over fifty years, but the full causal relation between LTP and memory storage remains debated; timing is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Causal link between LTP and memory remains debated
Collingridge's claim would be left out of a three-person prize
Limited direct disease-treatment consequences
